text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Subterranean complex may be built in Kent Ridge Park to house laboratories and offices.
- Small explosive device found aboard U.S. aircraft carrier in San Diego.
- Seven major local banks to have access to new source of cheap funds.
- Total of 2,300 terminals at 1,300 retail outlets will accept CashCard.
- One of world's biggest Chinese-owned companies, Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group, plans to invest U.S. $3 billion to $5 billion in China in the next three to five years.
- Economists say Singapore's economy picking up with gross domestic product growth to be about 4 percent in current quarter.
- Strong demand from systems integrators and computer vendors sends Intel's Pentium processor prices rising in Singapore in the past three months by some 30 to 60 percent.

- Property developers Malayan Credit Ltd and Habitat Properties plan to combine land from collective bungalow purchases in Grange Garden to be the biggest redevelopment site in Tanglin/Orchard Road area.
- Charoen Pokphand group is going high-tech with U.S.$1.2 billion wafer fabrication joint venture in Pudong development zone near Shanghai.
- Listed shipowner Osprey Maritime follows up quickly on landmark announcement to convert denomination of its listed shares from U.S. dollars to local currency.
